Subject: Re: Fwd: Data deletion request (usage logs + billing records)

Quick summary from finance perspective:

1) Invoices and the accounting ledger are statutory records. For US tax and audit requirements we typically retain accounting records for 7 years. For EU customers we advise retention aligned with local statutory retention (commonly 6 years, varies by jurisdiction).

2) "Usage logs" that are purely telemetry (request timestamps, token counts, anonymized model metadata) and not tied to identifiable user data can be removed according to our standard deletion process (default: 90 days for raw request logs, 2 years for aggregated billing summaries).

3) Records required for billing integrity (invoices, payment receipts, and entries in the billing ledger) must be preserved because they support revenue recognition and tax reporting. However, we can:
   - Provide redacted invoice PDFs that remove user emails/names while preserving invoice numbers, amounts, and dates;
   - Hash or replace customer internal IDs in the ledger export to a reversible token held by Finance, if necessary for internal audit but not accessible broadly;
   - Limit access to the preserved records to a narrow set of roles and mark them as "compliance-only".

Questions for legal: Is there any carve-out in the contract for OptiHealth that would change statutory retention obligations? Also, do we need to issue a formal letter explaining why we cannot remove certain accounting records?

Suggested customer reply (to be reviewed by Legal): short summary that invoices will be retained for statutory reasons but we can provide redacted versions and steps we will take to minimize identifiable data.

-Neha
Head of Finance Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data deletion request (usage logs + billing records)

Legal standpoint and proposed response: 

- Statutory retention: Neha is correct — accounting/journal entries and invoices are typically categorised as financial records. Deleting those would impair our ability to comply with tax, audit and contractual obligations. We therefore cannot fully delete invoice artifacts that are required for accounting and audit.

- Scope clarification: We should differentiate three buckets in our customer response:
  A) Billing ledger & invoice metadata (invoice numbers, amounts, dates) — preserved for statutory reasons; access restricted.
  B) Raw request-level usage logs that may contain PII — subject to deletion under OptiHealth's request where logs are identifiable to their users. We can delete these per policy and confirm completion with a deletion certificate.
  C) Aggregated billing summaries used for unit economics and billing reconciliation — can be retained but pseudonymized (replace customer-specific user identifiers with hashed tokens).

- Contract/PR: If OptiHealth's contract contains a narrower data retention clause that conflicts with statutory requirements, we should escalate to Legal & Finance to request a written exception or amendment.

- Customer-facing language (draft):

  Hi Anna,

  Thanks for the submission. We can comply with deletion requests for raw request logs and user-identifying telemetry and will issue a deletion certificate within our standard SLA (30 days) once you confirm the exact data scopes. 

  For accounting and tax reasons we must retain invoices and related ledger entries that support revenue recognition and audit trails. Where possible we will:
    • Provide redacted versions of invoices that remove user-level PII;
    • Pseudonymize identifiers in ledger exports; and
    • Restrict access to retained records to a limited set of Finance and Legal roles.

  If this approach is acceptable we will proceed with the deletion and provide a summary of retained artifacts. If you require a contract amendment to shorten financial retention windows, please let us know and we'll open that with Procurement.

  Laura Bennett
  Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
  Redwood Inference

Action items: Vanessa to confirm what the customer specifically wants deleted (invoices vs logs) so we scope the work and timeline. Finance to prepare redacted invoice example and ledger pseudonymization plan. Legal to prepare formal written notice.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data deletion request (usage logs + billing records)

Hi Anna — thanks for the request and for the form. Apologies for the back-and-forth; wanted to align internally first.

Short answer: we can delete user-identifying logs and telemetry that are not required for billing/audit (we will provide a deletion certificate once complete). For invoices and core ledger entries, Redwood must retain the records required for tax and audit.

Options we can offer right away (pick 1):
1) Full deletion of user-identifying request logs + redacted invoice copies (remove user emails/names; keep invoice numbers, dates, totals). Estimated completion: 30 days.
2) Full deletion of user-identifying request logs + ledger pseudonymization (replace internal IDs with hashed tokens) + access restrictions. Estimated completion: 45 days.
3) If OptiHealth requires an exception to have accounting records removed entirely, we'll need a contract amendment and sign-off from Procurement + Legal; this is a higher-friction option and may not be permitted for statutory reasons.

Please let us know which option you prefer and whether we should proceed with a redacted invoice example for your review (Neha will prepare).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
